nodes.name: Depth-first traversals
nodes.description: Visit the root before (preorder), between (inorder) or after (postorder) its subtrees; iteratively, an explicit stack replaces the call stack.

facets.explain: Explains what each order is useful for (copying, sorted output for BSTs, deleting).
facets.implement: Writes all three recursively with the visit in the right place.
facets.trace: Lists the visit order for a small tree.
facets.adapt: Writes the iterative versions, all three in one pass, and boundary traversal.

misconceptions.desc: Put the visit in the wrong place (wrote preorder when inorder was asked).
In iterative preorder, pushed the left child before the right, reversing the order.
In iterative inorder, popped before walking all the way left.
Iterative postorder visited a node before its right subtree was finished.
Kept the result in a global or static vector that is never cleared between calls.
In boundary traversal, added a leaf twice (as an edge node and as a leaf) or did not reverse the right edge.

nodes.name: Level-order traversal
nodes.description: Process a queue one level at a time by fixing the level's size before the inner loop.

facets.recognize: Uses BFS for anything per level: views, zigzag, width, nearest leaf.
facets.implement: Saves the level size, pushes only non-null children.
facets.trace: Can show the queue at the start of each level.
facets.adapt: Builds zigzag order, left and right views, and width with position indices.

misconceptions.desc: Used q.size() in the inner loop condition while pushing children, mixing levels.
Pushed null children and then dereferenced them.
For zigzag, reversed the order children are pushed instead of the level's output, breaking later levels.
For maximum width, numbered nodes 2i + 1 without rebasing each level, overflowing.

nodes.name: Bottom-up recursion
nodes.description: Each call returns what its parent needs (height, sum, a flag) and updates a global answer on the way up, so one pass is O(n).

facets.recognize: Sees when an answer at a node depends on values computed for both subtrees.
facets.explain: Explains why the returned value differs from the answer being tracked (height versus diameter).
facets.implement: Returns the parent's value and updates the answer in the same call.
facets.adapt: Signals failure with -1, drops negative paths with max(0, ...), returns several values at once.

misconceptions.desc: Called height() for every node inside another recursion (O(n²)).
Returned the answer instead of what the parent needs (the diameter instead of the height).
Added negative child path sums instead of taking max(0, ...).
Assumed the longest or best path passes through the root.
Counted nodes where edges were asked, or the reverse.

nodes.name: Comparing two trees
nodes.description: Recurse on two nodes at once: identical trees compare left with left; a symmetric tree compares left with right.

facets.explain: Explains why comparing traversals alone can miss shape differences.
facets.implement: Handles both null, one null, then compares values and the right pairs of children.

misconceptions.desc: Did not handle one node being null while the other is not.
For symmetry, compared left with left instead of left with right.
Compared traversal sequences without null markers, which can match for different shapes.

nodes.name: Vertical and horizontal coordinates
nodes.description: Give each node a (column, row): children are column - 1 and + 1. Group by column in an ordered map; level order decides which node a view sees first.

facets.implement: Tracks the column with each queued node and groups columns in a sorted map.
facets.adapt: Builds top view (first per column), bottom view (last per column) and vertical order with ties sorted by value.

misconceptions.desc: Used DFS for the top view, so a deeper node could be seen first in its column.
In vertical order, did not sort nodes with the same row and column by value.
Grouped columns in an unordered_map, so columns came out unsorted.

nodes.name: Root-to-node paths and lowest common ancestor
nodes.description: Find a path by pushing the node, recursing and popping when the target is not below; the LCA is where the two searches meet.

facets.explain: Explains why the first node with targets on different sides (or being one target) is the LCA.
facets.implement: Returns the found node up the recursion, popping path nodes on failure.

misconceptions.desc: Did not pop the node when the target was not below it.
Returned before checking both subtrees, so the LCA came out wrong.
Stored both root-to-target paths and compared them (O(n) space) where one recursion suffices.

nodes.name: Treating a tree as a graph
nodes.description: Record each node's parent, then BFS outward from a target through left, right and parent with a visited set.

facets.recognize: Sees that 'distance from a node' must also travel upward.
facets.implement: Builds the parent map, runs BFS with visited and counts levels.

misconceptions.desc: Searched only downward from the target, missing nodes reached through parents.
Did not mark visited nodes, so the search bounced between parent and child.
Counted time per node instead of per BFS level.

nodes.name: Building a tree from traversals
nodes.description: The preorder (or postorder) gives the root; its index in the inorder splits the left and right subtrees.

facets.explain: Explains why inorder plus preorder or postorder is unique, but preorder plus postorder is not.
facets.implement: Finds the root index with a map and computes subtree ranges from the left subtree size.

misconceptions.desc: Searched for the root in inorder linearly each time (O(n²)) instead of using a value -> index map.
Computed the subtree ranges wrongly (left size = root index - inorder start).
Believes preorder plus postorder determines a unique tree.
With postorder, built the left subtree first while consuming from the end.

nodes.name: Serializing a tree
nodes.description: Write nodes in level order (or preorder) with a marker for null, and read them back in the same order.

facets.implement: Writes and parses null markers and multi-digit, negative values.

misconceptions.desc: Left out null markers, so the shape could not be rebuilt.
Parsed values one character at a time, breaking on negative or multi-digit numbers.

nodes.name: Morris traversal
nodes.description: Thread each node's inorder predecessor back to it so the walk can return without a stack, then remove the thread: O(1) extra space.

facets.explain: Explains how the thread replaces the stack and why each edge is walked a constant number of times.
facets.implement: Creates and removes threads correctly for inorder.
facets.adapt: Writes Morris preorder and flattens a tree into a list in place.

misconceptions.desc: Did not remove the thread, leaving the tree modified or looping forever.
Visited at the wrong moment (preorder visits when creating the thread, inorder when removing it).
When flattening, linked nodes in the wrong order or left left pointers set.

nodes.name: Counting nodes of a complete tree
nodes.description: If the leftmost and rightmost heights match, the subtree is perfect and has 2^h - 1 nodes; otherwise recurse. O(log² n).

facets.explain: Explains why one of the two subtrees is always perfect.
facets.implement: Compares the two edge heights and uses (1 << h) - 1.

misconceptions.desc: Counted every node (O(n)) instead of using the complete-tree shortcut.
Computed 2^h off by one, or with an overflowing shift.
